assumptions: Scope is hobby/maker-grade low-voltage DC electronics and microcontroller work (Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi/Pico), not licensed mains or high-voltage engineering.
Nodes are concrete electronics/embedded work units, methods, or decision areas, each bounded to one heavy reasoning session.
No observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Basic electrical and power safety is in scope and treated as a hard foundation.
This subdomain sits under the parent domain Hardware, Microcontrollers & Self-Hosting.
exclusions: Licensed mains/AC wiring and high-voltage lab work.
PCB layout, fabrication, and design-for-manufacture at production scale.
Deep semiconductor device physics, RF design, and power-electronics topology design.
RTOS internals, FPGA design, and bare-metal driver-stack engineering beyond basics.
Cloud backend architecture and large-scale IoT fleet operations.

competency_questions.question: Before any hands-on work, what electrical, power, and battery safety rules and limits apply to this build?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ELECTRICAL_SAFETY yields a safety checklist and power limits

competency_questions.question: How are voltage, current, resistance, and power computed for a DC node before choosing parts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OHMS_LAW computes operating points and required values

competency_questions.question: Which components (passive and semiconductor) and series/parallel topology fit a required role under load?
How is a circuit captured as a schematic and prototyped on a breadboard or soldered?
How is a circuit measured and a fault localized with a multimeter during bring-up?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTIMETER_USE and DEBUG_TEST localize faults with measurement

competency_questions.question: How is clean, sized, regulated power provided and budgeted for the project?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POWER_SUPPLY produces regulated rails within a budget

competency_questions.question: Which microcontroller board fits the I/O, connectivity, voltage, and power needs?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MCU_SELECTION chooses a board and voltage domain

competency_questions.question: How are GPIO pins configured and firmware written to drive inputs and outputs safely?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GPIO_INTERFACING and FIRMWARE_BASICS configure and program pins

competency_questions.question: How are analog signals read and proportional outputs generated (ADC and PWM)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANALOG_IO and PWM_CONTROL handle analog input and proportional output

competency_questions.question: How are sensors and actuators selected, driven, and validated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SENSOR_INTEGRATION and ACTUATOR_DRIVE integrate and protect I/O devices

competency_questions.question: How are peripherals connected over I2C/SPI/UART and wireless links?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIGITAL_BUSES and CONNECTIVITY_IOT handle wired and wireless links

competency_questions.question: How is a build brought up incrementally and integrated into a finished project?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEBUG_TEST and PROJECT_INTEGRATION stage bring-up and integration

competency_questions.question: What acceptance criteria mark the finished build as safe and working?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROJECT_INTEGRATION and ELECTRICAL_SAFETY define final acceptance

competency_questions.question: Where are authoritative component facts (datasheets, pinouts, reference designs) found and trusted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DATASHEET_SOURCING grounds component decisions in authoritative sources

glossary.definition: V=IR with power P=VI; the core relation linking voltage, current, and resistance in a DC node
a capacitor placed at a power pin to supply transient current and quiet the rail
a diode across an inductive load that clamps back-EMF when current is switched off
the nominal logic level family of a board/part, typically 3.3V or 5V
a general-purpose digital pin configurable as input or output within current/voltage limits
a digital signal whose duty cycle encodes a proportional value for dimming, speed, or servo position
a two-wire addressable serial bus (SDA/SCL) needing pull-ups, for connecting multiple peripherals
an MCU reset or malfunction caused by the supply rail dipping below a minimum voltage
a transistor/H-bridge/IC between a logic pin and a real load that carries the load current
the manufacturer document giving a part's ratings, pinout, and recommended circuits

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established hobby-electronics and embedded references (Platt 'Make: Electronics'; Monk 'Programming Arduino'; Banzi & Shiloh 'Getting Started with Arduino') plus standard datasheet/maker practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Establish basic electrical, power, and battery safety rules before any hands-on work: voltage limits, current limits, isolation, short-circuit and lithium-battery hazards.
contradictors: builder who powers a circuit before checking shorts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-voltage source, mains, or lithium chemistry enters the project

pros.claim: a short safety pass prevents fires, ruined boards, and injury
pros.example: add a fuse and check for shorts before first power-up

cons.claim: over-cautious limits can stall harmless 5V prototyping
cons.example: refusing to touch any battery slows a coin-cell project

failure_modes: no current limit on first power-up
acceptance_tests: power source within rated limits and fused
short-circuit check passed before power
lithium cells handled per chemistry rules

nodes.definition: Apply the voltage/current/resistance relationship (V=IR) and power (P=VI) to reason about any DC node before choosing components.
contradictors: builder who guesses resistor values

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a circuit's supply, load, or topology changes the operating point

pros.claim: correct V/I/R math sizes every later component
pros.example: compute an LED resistor from supply, Vf, and target current

cons.claim: DC-only reasoning misleads on AC or switching nodes
cons.example: applying V=IR to an inductor's transient

acceptance_tests: units consistent across the calculation
power rating checked for each resistor

nodes.definition: Select and read passive components (resistors, capacitors, inductors) by value, tolerance, rating, and package for a given circuit role.
contradictors: builder who omits decoupling caps

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a supply rail, signal speed, or current rating changes the passive requirements

pros.claim: right passives stabilize rails and shape signals
pros.example: add 100nF decoupling at each IC power pin

cons.claim: wrong rating fails silently or catastrophically
cons.example: an electrolytic under-rated for voltage bulges

acceptance_tests: each passive value, tolerance, and rating matches its role

nodes.definition: Use diodes and transistors (BJT/MOSFET) for rectification, protection, switching, and amplification, respecting biasing and ratings.
contradictors: builder who drives a relay with no flyback diode

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the switched load, control level, or current rating changes

pros.claim: a transistor switch lets a logic pin drive real loads
pros.example: a MOSFET low-side switch drives a 12V fan from a GPIO

cons.claim: missing protection diodes destroy parts on inductive turn-off
cons.example: relay back-EMF kills a driver transistor

failure_modes: no flyback diode on inductive load
acceptance_tests: device ratings exceed worst-case load
gate/base drive adequate for full switching

nodes.definition: Compose components into series and parallel circuit blocks (dividers, current paths, power distribution) and reason about their combined behavior.
contradictors: builder who powers parallel loads off one weak rail

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when blocks are added/removed or rail loading changes

pros.claim: topology choice sets which loads can share a rail
pros.example: split a noisy motor rail from a clean sensor rail

cons.claim: naive voltage dividers sag under load current
cons.example: a divider biasing a transistor collapses when loaded

acceptance_tests: each rail's total load within source capability
ground return paths planned

nodes.definition: Read and draw schematic diagrams: symbols, nets, reference designators, and power/ground conventions to communicate a circuit unambiguously.
contradictors: builder who wires from memory with no schematic

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the circuit design or pin assignment changes

pros.claim: a clear schematic makes wiring and debugging reproducible
pros.example: trace a fault by following nets on the schematic

cons.claim: over-detailed schematics slow quick breadboard sketches
cons.example: drafting a full schematic for a two-part test

acceptance_tests: every net and component labeled
power and ground explicit

nodes.definition: Build a temporary circuit on a solderless breadboard from a schematic: rail wiring, component placement, and jumper discipline for quick iteration.
contradictors: builder who breadboards high-current motor drivers

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the prototype is moved toward a soldered build or higher current

pros.claim: breadboards make iteration fast and reversible
pros.example: swap a resistor in seconds to test a bias point

cons.claim: breadboards add contact resistance and noise, failing at high speed/current
cons.example: a 1A motor path browns out through breadboard contacts

acceptance_tests: rails powered and verified
no high-current paths on the breadboard

nodes.definition: Produce reliable solder joints on through-hole and basic SMD parts: iron control, joint inspection, and desoldering for permanent assembly.
contradictors: builder who tolerates cold joints

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when joints fail inspection or the assembly must be reworked

pros.claim: solid joints make a build durable and portable
pros.example: a soldered sensor survives vibration a breadboard would not

cons.claim: soldering is hard to reverse and burns parts if mishandled
cons.example: overheating lifts a PCB pad permanently

acceptance_tests: joints shiny and mechanically sound
no bridges between adjacent pads
continuity verified

nodes.definition: Measure voltage, current, resistance, and continuity with a multimeter to verify a circuit against its expected values.
contradictors: builder who debugs by guessing instead of measuring

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when measured values diverge from expected or a new fault appears

pros.claim: measurement turns guessing into evidence-based debugging
pros.example: confirm a 3.3V rail actually reads 3.28V at the chip

cons.claim: wrong range or current-mode misuse blows the meter fuse
cons.example: measuring voltage with leads still in the current jack shorts the supply

failure_modes: meter in current mode across a source
acceptance_tests: meter mode and range match the measurement
expected vs measured compared per net

nodes.definition: Provide and regulate clean power for a project: source selection, linear/switching regulators, decoupling, and a power budget.
contradictors: builder who powers a 3.3V board from 5V directly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when load current, source, or rail voltage requirements change

pros.claim: a sized, regulated supply prevents brownouts and damage
pros.example: a 3.3V LDO with enough headroom keeps an ESP32 stable

cons.claim: a wrong rail voltage instantly destroys logic parts
cons.example: feeding 5V to a 3.3V-only sensor lets out the magic smoke

failure_modes: wrong rail voltage to a board
acceptance_tests: each rail within board/component voltage limits
supply current margin above peak load
regulator thermal within limit

nodes.definition: Choose a microcontroller board (Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi Pico, or Raspberry Pi) by I/O, connectivity, voltage, and compute needs of the project.

excluded: custom MCU silicon selection for mass production

contradictors: builder who picks a board before knowing I/O needs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when I/O, connectivity, power, or voltage-domain requirements change

pros.claim: matching the board to needs avoids redesign
pros.example: pick ESP32 when WiFi is required instead of bolting on a module

cons.claim: a 5V vs 3.3V mismatch propagates into every interface
cons.example: choosing a 5V Uno forces level shifting for 3.3V sensors

acceptance_tests: board I/O and peripherals cover the requirement
logic voltage domain decided and documented

nodes.definition: Interface digital GPIO pins to the outside world safely: input modes, pull-ups/downs, output drive limits, and logic-level matching.
contradictors: builder who sinks 50mA straight from a GPIO

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a pin's role, external level, or drive requirement changes

pros.claim: correct pin config prevents floating inputs and fried pins
pros.example: enable an internal pull-up so a button reads cleanly

cons.claim: exceeding pin current or feeding 5V to a 3.3V pin damages the MCU
cons.example: driving an LED with no resistor overloads the GPIO

acceptance_tests: each pin within current and voltage limits
inputs have defined pull state

nodes.definition: Write basic microcontroller firmware: setup/loop structure, timing, reading inputs and driving outputs, and the upload/flash cycle.
contradictors: builder who blocks the loop with long delays

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when behavior, timing budget, or peripheral set changes

pros.claim: non-blocking firmware keeps inputs and outputs responsive
pros.example: use millis() timing so a button still responds while an LED blinks

cons.claim: blocking delays freeze the whole loop and miss events
cons.example: a delay(1000) drops button presses for a second

acceptance_tests: firmware compiles and uploads to the target board
timing-critical paths are non-blocking

nodes.definition: Read analog signals via the ADC and produce analog-like outputs: reference voltage, resolution, sampling, and scaling to real units.
contradictors: builder who treats raw ADC counts as volts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the sensor range, ADC reference, or required accuracy changes

pros.claim: correct reference and scaling turn ADC counts into real units
pros.example: scale a 0-1023 read into 0-5V then into a temperature

cons.claim: a wrong reference or noisy input corrupts every reading
cons.example: a floating ADC reference makes readings drift

acceptance_tests: raw counts scaled to correct units with the right reference
input within ADC range

nodes.definition: Generate PWM to control brightness, motor speed, or servo position via duty cycle and frequency, with appropriate output stages.
contradictors: builder who drives a motor straight from a PWM pin

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the actuator, PWM frequency, or drive current changes

pros.claim: PWM gives proportional control from a digital pin
pros.example: dim an LED smoothly by varying duty cycle

cons.claim: wrong frequency or direct drive damages the actuator or pin
cons.example: servo jitter from a wrong PWM period

failure_modes: direct motor drive off a pin
no driver between pin and load
acceptance_tests: PWM frequency and duty match the actuator spec
a driver stage isolates the pin from the load

nodes.definition: Select sensors and integrate them electrically and in firmware: interface type, signal conditioning, power, and reading validation.
contradictors: builder who trusts unvalidated sensor output

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the measured quantity, interface, or accuracy requirement changes

pros.claim: the right sensor and interface make data trustworthy
pros.example: choose an I2C temp sensor with a known driver over a raw thermistor when accuracy matters

cons.claim: an unconditioned or mis-wired sensor yields garbage data
cons.example: a thermistor with no fixed reference reads nonsense

acceptance_tests: sensor interface matches the board's bus/levels
readings validated against a known reference

nodes.definition: Drive motors and actuators (DC, stepper, servo, relays) through proper driver stages, isolation, and power, never directly from logic pins.
contradictors: builder who drives a motor directly from a GPIO

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when actuator current, type, or power source changes

pros.claim: a driver stage protects the MCU and delivers real power
pros.example: an H-bridge runs a DC motor both directions off a separate rail

cons.claim: direct or unprotected drive destroys the MCU and parts
cons.example: back-EMF from a relay coil kills an unprotected pin

failure_modes: shared rail browns out the MCU
acceptance_tests: actuator driven through a rated driver, not a logic pin
inductive loads have flyback protection
motor power separated from logic power

nodes.definition: Use I2C, SPI, and UART buses to connect peripherals: addressing, pull-ups, chip-select, clock/level matching, and bus debugging.
contradictors: builder who omits I2C pull-up resistors

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a peripheral, bus type, or logic level changes

pros.claim: standard buses connect many peripherals on few pins
pros.example: hang several I2C sensors on one two-wire bus by address

cons.claim: missing pull-ups or level mismatch silently breaks the bus
cons.example: a 5V SPI device corrupts data to a 3.3V MCU

acceptance_tests: bus pull-ups and levels correct for all devices
addresses and chip-selects unique

nodes.definition: Systematically bring up and debug a build: isolate power, verify rails, test subsystems incrementally, and localize hardware vs firmware faults.
contradictors: builder who powers the full board and hopes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new fault appears or a subsystem fails bring-up

pros.claim: incremental bring-up localizes faults fast and safely
pros.example: power only the regulator first and confirm rails before adding the MCU

cons.claim: powering everything at once hides which stage failed
cons.example: a full power-up smokes a part with no clue which one

failure_modes: no rail verification before adding loads
firmware blamed for a hardware fault
acceptance_tests: each subsystem verified before the next is powered
rails confirmed before adding loads
fault localized to hardware or firmware

nodes.definition: Integrate verified subsystems into a finished project: wiring harness, mechanical mounting, enclosure, power-on behavior, and final acceptance.
contradictors: builder who boxes up an unverified build

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a subsystem changes or the integrated build fails acceptance

pros.claim: integration on verified subsystems yields a robust finished build
pros.example: mount and wire only sensors that already passed bring-up

cons.claim: integrating unverified parts multiplies fault sources and rework
cons.example: an enclosure traps an intermittent joint that is hard to reach

acceptance_tests: only verified subsystems integrated
power-on behavior matches acceptance criteria
thermal and mechanical fit checked

nodes.definition: Find and read authoritative datasheets, pinouts, and reference designs, and source genuine parts to ground every component decision.
contradictors: builder who wires a part from a forum post, not its datasheet

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a part is substituted or a rating/pinout assumption is questioned

pros.claim: datasheets ground decisions in authoritative limits and pinouts
pros.example: confirm a regulator's dropout and max current before trusting it

cons.claim: clone boards and bad listings diverge from the canonical datasheet
cons.example: a clone sensor uses a different I2C address than the datasheet

failure_modes: wiring from a forum instead of the datasheet
clone behaves unlike the genuine part
acceptance_tests: each critical rating and pin sourced from the official datasheet
part substitution checked against the datasheet

nodes.definition: Add wireless connectivity (WiFi/BLE on ESP32) and basic IoT messaging so an embedded build can report data or take commands over a network.
contradictors: builder who hardcodes WiFi credentials in shared code

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the network, broker, or power budget for connectivity changes

pros.claim: wireless messaging turns a local build into a reporting IoT node
pros.example: an ESP32 publishes sensor readings over MQTT to a self-hosted broker

cons.claim: radio adds power draw, reconnection bugs, and credential-handling risk
cons.example: WiFi reconnection stalls block the main loop

failure_modes: radio power spikes brown out the rail
acceptance_tests: connectivity brings up and recovers from disconnects
credentials kept out of shared/version-controlled code

edges.why_related: V/I/R math sets the values passives must hit
edges.benefit_of_coupling: passives sized to real operating points
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking passive values before doing the math wastes the build
edges.example: compute an LED resistor before buying it
edges.resolution_rule: do the Ohm's-law math before selecting passives

edges.why_related: biasing and ratings come from V/I/R reasoning
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbiased devices saturate or burn
edges.example: size a base resistor from current gain
edges.resolution_rule: fix operating-point math before choosing a transistor

edges.why_related: series/parallel math underlies topology choices
edges.benefit_of_coupling: rails and dividers behave as intended
edges.risk_of_conflict: topology drawn without load math sags
edges.example: check a divider under its real load
edges.resolution_rule: do load math before fixing topology

edges.why_related: topology is built from selected passives
edges.benefit_of_coupling: blocks composed of correctly rated parts
edges.risk_of_conflict: topology with wrong parts must be reworked
edges.example: place decoupling per IC in the topology
edges.resolution_rule: select passives before composing topology

edges.why_related: the schematic documents the chosen topology
edges.risk_of_conflict: an undocumented topology is unbuildable reliably
edges.example: draw the rail plan as a schematic
edges.resolution_rule: fix topology before drawing the schematic

edges.why_related: the breadboard is built from the schematic
edges.risk_of_conflict: building from memory wires the wrong net
edges.example: follow net labels onto the breadboard
edges.resolution_rule: build the breadboard from an approved schematic

edges.why_related: safety rules bound how the breadboard may be powered
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unsafe power-up damages parts or person
edges.example: fuse and short-check before first power
edges.resolution_rule: apply safety limits before powering the prototype

edges.why_related: validate on a breadboard before committing to solder
edges.risk_of_conflict: soldering an unproven circuit is costly rework
edges.example: prove the bias on breadboard then solder
edges.resolution_rule: verify on breadboard before soldering

edges.why_related: safety bounds iron, fumes, and powered-rework practice
edges.risk_of_conflict: burns or fume exposure from unsafe practice
edges.example: never solder a powered high-current rail
edges.resolution_rule: follow safety rules during assembly

edges.why_related: measurements are interpreted against V/I/R expectations
edges.risk_of_conflict: readings without expectations are meaningless
edges.example: predict a node voltage then measure it
edges.resolution_rule: derive expected values before measuring

edges.why_related: safe-measurement rules bound meter use
edges.benefit_of_coupling: measurements taken without hazard or meter damage
edges.risk_of_conflict: current-mode misuse shorts the supply
edges.example: keep leads out of the current jack for voltage
edges.resolution_rule: apply safe measurement rules before probing

edges.why_related: power budgeting uses current and dissipation math
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unsized supply browns out or overheats
edges.example: sum load currents to size the regulator
edges.resolution_rule: do the power-budget math before fixing the supply

edges.why_related: regulators need correct decoupling/filter passives
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing caps make a regulator oscillate
edges.example: add the datasheet's output cap
edges.resolution_rule: place required passives before trusting the rail

edges.why_related: safety bounds source voltage, current, and battery use
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unsafe rail damages everything downstream
edges.example: fuse the battery and limit current
edges.resolution_rule: apply safety limits before energizing rails

edges.why_related: voltage-domain safety constrains board choice
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a board whose levels suit the design safely
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring 3.3V/5V domain forces risky shifting
edges.example: pick a 3.3V board for 3.3V sensors
edges.resolution_rule: decide the voltage domain under safety rules before choosing a board

edges.why_related: the board's pinout and levels define pin interfacing
edges.risk_of_conflict: interfacing planned for the wrong board fails
edges.example: map roles onto the chosen board's pinout
edges.resolution_rule: select the board before planning pin interfacing

edges.why_related: available power constrains viable boards
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a board the supply can actually run
edges.risk_of_conflict: a hungry board browns out a weak supply
edges.example: match a Pi's current draw to the supply
edges.resolution_rule: check the power budget against the board

edges.why_related: pin current/resistor math protects pins
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-current math errors fry pins
edges.example: size an LED resistor for a 3.3V pin
edges.resolution_rule: apply pin current math before wiring GPIO

edges.why_related: firmware drives the configured pins
edges.benefit_of_coupling: code matches the real pin configuration
edges.risk_of_conflict: code against wrong pin config misbehaves
edges.example: read the button on its configured pin
edges.resolution_rule: fix pin configuration before writing firmware

edges.why_related: ADC pins are a special case of pin interfacing
edges.risk_of_conflict: an out-of-range analog input corrupts reads
edges.example: wire a sensor to an ADC-capable pin
edges.resolution_rule: configure the pin domain before analog reads

edges.why_related: buses run over configured GPIO with pull-ups/levels
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing pull-ups break the bus
edges.example: add I2C pull-ups on the bus pins
edges.resolution_rule: configure bus pins before using the bus

edges.why_related: PWM is generated and tuned in firmware
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong PWM config jitters the actuator
edges.example: set the servo period in firmware
edges.resolution_rule: get firmware basics working before PWM

edges.why_related: a transistor driver stage carries the PWM load
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the load driven, not the pin
edges.risk_of_conflict: direct PWM drive overloads the pin
edges.example: drive a motor via a MOSFET from PWM
edges.resolution_rule: add a driver stage before PWM-driving a load

edges.why_related: analog sensors are read through the ADC path
edges.risk_of_conflict: unscaled analog reads give bad data
edges.example: scale a thermistor read to temperature
edges.resolution_rule: establish the analog path before integrating analog sensors

edges.why_related: bus sensors are integrated over I2C/SPI
edges.benefit_of_coupling: digital sensors talk to the MCU
edges.risk_of_conflict: bus errors hide as bad sensor data
edges.example: read an I2C sensor at its address
edges.resolution_rule: bring up the bus before integrating bus sensors

edges.why_related: actuator drivers are built from discrete/driver semiconductors
edges.risk_of_conflict: weak drive devices fail under load
edges.example: use an H-bridge rated for the motor
edges.resolution_rule: choose adequate driver devices before driving actuators

edges.why_related: actuators need their own sized power rail
edges.benefit_of_coupling: actuators powered without browning out logic
edges.risk_of_conflict: a shared weak rail resets the MCU
edges.example: give the motor its own rail
edges.resolution_rule: size and separate actuator power before driving

edges.why_related: safety bounds motor power, isolation, and protection
edges.risk_of_conflict: unprotected inductive drive injures parts/person
edges.example: add flyback and isolate motor power
edges.resolution_rule: apply protection and isolation rules before driving actuators

edges.why_related: debugging relies on measurement to localize faults
edges.risk_of_conflict: guess-debugging without measurement wanders
edges.example: measure rails before adding loads
edges.resolution_rule: measure during bring-up, do not guess

edges.why_related: firmware logging supports bring-up diagnostics
edges.risk_of_conflict: blaming firmware for a hardware fault misleads
edges.example: add serial logging during bring-up
edges.resolution_rule: use firmware diagnostics to isolate faults

edges.why_related: integration consumes verified, debugged subsystems
edges.risk_of_conflict: integrating unverified parts multiplies faults
edges.example: integrate only bring-up-passed modules
edges.resolution_rule: finish debugging before integration

edges.why_related: the final build uses soldered, durable assemblies
edges.risk_of_conflict: loose joints fail in the enclosure
edges.example: solder and inspect before boxing up
edges.resolution_rule: solder and verify joints before integration

edges.why_related: integrated systems include validated sensors
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unvalidated sensor taints the system
edges.example: integrate only validated sensor paths
edges.resolution_rule: validate sensors before system integration

edges.why_related: integrated systems include protected actuator drives
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unprotected drive risks the whole build
edges.example: integrate only protected actuator stages
edges.resolution_rule: verify actuator drive before integration

edges.why_related: device ratings and pinouts come from datasheets
edges.risk_of_conflict: wiring from memory exceeds true ratings
edges.example: read the MOSFET datasheet for Vgs and Id
edges.resolution_rule: ground device use in its datasheet

edges.why_related: sensor interface and addresses come from datasheets
edges.risk_of_conflict: clone sensors diverge from the datasheet
edges.example: confirm the I2C address from the datasheet
edges.resolution_rule: verify sensor specs against the datasheet

edges.why_related: regulator limits and app circuits come from datasheets
edges.risk_of_conflict: exceeding dropout/current from guesswork fails
edges.example: use the regulator's recommended caps
edges.resolution_rule: ground the supply design in the datasheet

edges.why_related: clean logic power and noisy high-current actuation compete on one supply
edges.risk_of_conflict: sharing one rail couples motor noise into logic
edges.example: a motor inrush dips the MCU rail and resets it
edges.resolution_rule: split rails or add bulk/decoupling; never share a weak rail

edges.why_related: pressure to finish integration competes with thorough bring-up
edges.risk_of_conflict: skipping bring-up to integrate hides faults
edges.example: boxing up before measuring traps a fault
edges.resolution_rule: bring-up rigor dominates schedule pressure before integration

edges.why_related: safety and thermal limits bound the finished, enclosed build
edges.risk_of_conflict: an enclosure that traps heat or a short is hazardous
edges.example: ensure vent and fusing in the enclosure
edges.resolution_rule: apply safety/thermal limits before closing the build

conflict_axes.trigger: deadline pressure tempts skipping fusing, short-checks, or staged power-up
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: electrical/power safety dominates build speed for any power source above coin-cell or any lithium pack
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a build would be powered without short-check or fusing on a real battery
conflict_axes.example: first power-up of a LiPo build with no fuse to save time

conflict_axes.trigger: one supply is cheaper but couples motor noise/inrush into logic
resolution_order: share only if margin is proven
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: separate/isolated actuator power dominates a single shared rail whenever motor inrush can dip the logic rail
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: MCU resets correlate with actuator activation
conflict_axes.example: a servo inrush browns out the MCU on a shared 5V rail

conflict_axes.trigger: simple delay()-based code is easy but starves timed peripherals
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: non-blocking timing dominates blocking simplicity on any path with PWM, bus, or input-timing requirements
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: events or bus reads are dropped during delays
conflict_axes.example: a delay(1000) makes a button and an I2C poll both miss their windows

conflict_axes.trigger: breadboards are reversible but unreliable at speed/current; solder is durable but hard to undo
resolution_order: commit to solder only after validation
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validation-before-commit dominates: do not solder a circuit not yet proven on breadboard
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a circuit is being soldered before its bias/behavior is verified
conflict_axes.example: soldering an unproven sensor board then finding the divider was wrong

conflict_axes.trigger: mixing 3.3V and 5V parts forces level shifting or risks damage
resolution_order: decide the dominant logic domain early
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the chosen logic-voltage domain dominates; cross-domain signals must be explicitly level-shifted
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a 5V signal would reach a 3.3V-only pin
conflict_axes.example: a 5V Uno reading a 3.3V sensor without a level shifter risks the sensor

conflict_axes.trigger: swapping parts by guesswork is faster than measuring but wanders
resolution_order: change one variable at a time
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: measured evidence dominates guess-and-swap debugging for any non-trivial fault
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: parts are being replaced with no measurement narrowing the fault
conflict_axes.example: replacing a working sensor because the real fault was a cold joint

conflict_axes.trigger: forum/AI snippets are fast but may contradict the authoritative datasheet
resolution_order: check the official datasheet for ratings/pinout
use community examples only as hints
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the official datasheet dominates forum lore for ratings, pinouts, and addresses
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a critical rating or pinout is taken from a forum post against the datasheet
conflict_axes.example: trusting a forum pinout that swaps SDA/SCL versus the datasheet

conflict_axes.trigger: adding radios/peripherals raises current draw beyond the supply/battery budget
resolution_order: size the power budget for peak draw
trim or stage features to fit
upgrade the supply only within safety limits
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the power and safety budget dominates feature ambition; features must fit the achievable, safe budget
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: peak current with all features exceeds the supply or battery safe limit
conflict_axes.example: enabling WiFi pushes peak current past a small LDO's rating

conflict_axes.trigger: finishing the enclosure fast competes with fully verifying each subsystem first
resolution_order: leave faults accessible until final acceptance
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: subsystem verification dominates integration speed; unverified subsystems are not integrated
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an enclosure would trap an unverified or intermittent subsystem
conflict_axes.example: boxing up a build with an intermittent joint that is then unreachable

edge_cases.trigger: a motor/relay/high-current load is wired straight to a logic pin
edge_cases.failure_mode: GPIO over-current destroys the MCU pin or board
edge_cases.example: a DC motor connected directly to a digital output pin
edge_cases.detection_method: check that every load above the pin current limit goes through a rated driver stage

edge_cases.trigger: an inductive load is switched with no flyback/clamp diode
edge_cases.failure_mode: back-EMF spike destroys the switching device
edge_cases.example: a relay coil switched by a bare transistor with no diode
edge_cases.detection_method: verify every inductive load has a flyback or clamp path in the schematic
resolution: add a flyback diode across the coil
use a driver IC with built-in clamps

edge_cases.failure_mode: over-voltage damages the pin or corrupts bus data
edge_cases.example: a 5V SPI master driving a 3.3V sensor with no level shift
edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check every signal crossing a voltage-domain boundary for a level shifter
resolution: add level shifting at the boundary

edge_cases.trigger: voltage is measured with leads still in the current jack
edge_cases.failure_mode: the meter shorts the source and blows its fuse or the supply
edge_cases.example: probing a rail with the red lead in the 10A jack
edge_cases.detection_method: confirm meter mode and lead jack match the quantity before probing a powered node
resolution: move leads to the voltage jacks

edge_cases.trigger: actuator inrush dips a shared rail below the MCU's brownout threshold
edge_cases.failure_mode: the MCU resets or behaves erratically when the actuator activates
edge_cases.example: a stepper inrush resets the board on a shared 5V rail
edge_cases.detection_method: correlate MCU resets with actuator activation and measure rail dip under load

edge_cases.trigger: an I2C bus has no pull-up resistors
edge_cases.failure_mode: the bus never communicates and reads as dead
edge_cases.example: two I2C sensors wired with no pull-ups on SDA/SCL
edge_cases.detection_method: verify pull-ups exist and match bus speed before debugging the protocol

edge_cases.trigger: a digital input has no defined pull state
edge_cases.failure_mode: the input reads random noise and misfires logic
edge_cases.example: a button input with no pull-up reading random highs/lows
edge_cases.detection_method: check every input pin has a pull-up/down (internal or external) defined

edge_cases.trigger: long blocking delays stall the main loop
edge_cases.failure_mode: inputs, PWM updates, and bus reads are missed during delays
edge_cases.example: a delay(2000) freezes input handling for two seconds
edge_cases.detection_method: scan firmware for blocking delays on timing-critical paths

edge_cases.trigger: ADC counts are scaled with the wrong reference voltage
edge_cases.failure_mode: all derived readings are systematically wrong
edge_cases.example: treating 0-1023 as 0-5V when the reference is 3.3V
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the scaling uses the actual ADC reference and the input stays in range
resolution: use the correct reference in scaling

edge_cases.trigger: a clone part behaves unlike the genuine datasheet (address, timing, pinout)
edge_cases.failure_mode: firmware written to the datasheet fails on the clone
edge_cases.example: a clone sensor responding on a different I2C address
edge_cases.detection_method: scan the bus and compare actual behavior against the datasheet for clone parts
resolution: adjust firmware or source a genuine part

edge_cases.trigger: a cold or intermittent solder joint passes initial test then fails
edge_cases.failure_mode: an intermittent fault appears after the build is enclosed
edge_cases.example: a sensor that drops out only when the case is flexed
edge_cases.detection_method: inspect and reflow suspect joints and test under flex/vibration before enclosing

workflow.objective: set electrical/power safety limits before any hands-on work
acceptance_tests: power source rated and fused; short-check defined
workflow.do_first_because: safety is the irreversible foundation every powered step inherits

workflow.objective: compute operating points and fix circuit topology
acceptance_tests: V/I/R and power computed; rails within source capability
workflow.do_first_because: all component sizing depends on correct V/I/R math and topology

workflow.objective: select and ground every component in its datasheet
acceptance_tests: each critical part rating/pinout sourced from its datasheet
workflow.do_first_because: parts chosen against datasheets prevent rating and pinout rework

workflow.objective: capture the schematic and build a breadboard prototype
acceptance_tests: every net labeled; prototype matches schematic
workflow.do_first_because: a documented prototype makes later debugging and soldering reproducible

workflow.objective: provide regulated power and select the microcontroller board
acceptance_tests: rails within board limits; current margin above peak; voltage domain decided
workflow.do_first_because: board and rail choices are high-coupling foundations for all firmware and I/O

workflow.objective: configure pins and write basic firmware
acceptance_tests: pins within limits; firmware compiles and uploads; timing-critical paths non-blocking
workflow.do_first_because: pin configuration and firmware structure gate every I/O behavior

workflow.objective: bring up analog input and proportional PWM output
acceptance_tests: ADC scaled to units with correct reference; PWM matches actuator spec
workflow.do_first_because: validated signal paths are prerequisites for trustworthy sensor/actuator work

workflow.objective: integrate buses, sensors, actuators, and connectivity
acceptance_tests: bus pull-ups/levels correct; actuators driven through rated drivers with protection; sensors validated
workflow.do_first_because: peripherals depend on validated signals, power, and protected drive stages

workflow.objective: bring up incrementally, debug with measurement, and solder verified circuits
acceptance_tests: each subsystem verified before the next is powered; joints inspected and continuous
workflow.do_first_because: measured, incremental bring-up localizes faults before they are hidden by integration

workflow.objective: integrate verified subsystems and run final safety/acceptance tests
acceptance_tests: only verified subsystems integrated; power-on behavior meets acceptance; thermal/mechanical and safety checks pass
workflow.do_first_because: integration on verified subsystems under safety limits yields a robust finished build

dominance_rules.trigger: a powered step is requested before safety checks (fusing, short-check, staged power-up) complete
dominance_rules.rule: electrical/power safety dominates build speed for any real power source
dominance_rules.required_action: block first power-up until ELECTRICAL_SAFETY checks pass
dominance_rules.example: refuse to power a LiPo build with no fuse to hit a deadline

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is sequenced before an unmet electrical prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: true dependency precedence dominates value-first ordering
dominance_rules.required_action: reorder so prerequisites (math, power, board) precede dependents
dominance_rules.example: size the supply before integrating the actuator it powers

dominance_rules.trigger: a critical rating, pinout, or address is taken from a forum/AI snippet against the datasheet
dominance_rules.rule: the official datasheet dominates community lore for authoritative facts
dominance_rules.required_action: replace the lore value with the datasheet value and re-verify
dominance_rules.example: use the datasheet I2C address, not a forum's wrong one

dominance_rules.trigger: parts are swapped by guesswork with no measurement narrowing the fault
dominance_rules.required_action: form an expected value and measure before replacing any part
dominance_rules.example: measure the rail before blaming the sensor

dominance_rules.trigger: a load above the pin current limit would be driven directly from a logic pin
dominance_rules.rule: a rated driver stage dominates direct pin drive for any real load
dominance_rules.required_action: insert a transistor/H-bridge/driver IC and protection before driving the load
dominance_rules.example: drive the motor via an H-bridge, never the GPIO

dominance_rules.trigger: actuator and logic would share a rail whose margin cannot absorb inrush
dominance_rules.rule: separate/decoupled actuator power dominates a weak shared rail
dominance_rules.required_action: split rails or add proven bulk decoupling before sharing
dominance_rules.example: give the stepper its own rail to stop MCU resets

dominance_rules.trigger: an unverified subsystem would be integrated or enclosed
dominance_rules.required_action: integrate only subsystems that passed bring-up; keep faults accessible
dominance_rules.example: do not box up a build with an intermittent joint

dominance_rules.trigger: blocking delays sit on timing-critical PWM/bus/input paths
dominance_rules.rule: non-blocking timing dominates blocking simplicity on timing-critical paths
dominance_rules.required_action: convert blocking delays to non-blocking timing on those paths
dominance_rules.example: replace delay() with millis() so the bus poll is not starved

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk action (soldering, mains, lithium, final close) is taken without review
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible/high-risk actions
dominance_rules.required_action: require human review before any node with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 is finalized
dominance_rules.example: review the actuator drive design before energizing the motor

dominance_rules.trigger: a build or subsystem is being locked/closed before acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.rule: passing acceptance tests dominates locking the build
dominance_rules.required_action: block enclosure/sign-off until acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.example: hold final close until power-on behavior meets criteria

anti_rework_rules.rule: set electrical/power safety limits before any powered work
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unsafe power-up can destroy the whole build, forcing a restart
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a real power source is energized before the safety checklist passes
anti_rework_rules.example: powering a battery build before any short-check

anti_rework_rules.rule: compute V/I/R and power before selecting components
anti_rework_rules.rationale: parts chosen without the math get re-bought and re-soldered
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: components are ordered before any operating-point calculation
anti_rework_rules.example: buying resistors before computing the LED current

anti_rework_rules.rule: ground each critical part in its datasheet before wiring it
anti_rework_rules.rationale: wiring from memory or lore causes pinout and rating rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a part is wired from a forum pinout, not its datasheet
anti_rework_rules.example: swapping SDA/SCL because a forum diagram was wrong

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix circuit topology before drawing the schematic
anti_rework_rules.rationale: redrawing a schematic after a topology change is wasted work
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: schematic capture begins before topology is settled
anti_rework_rules.example: redrawing nets after moving a divider

anti_rework_rules.rule: capture a schematic before breadboarding or soldering
anti_rework_rules.rationale: building from memory wires wrong nets and forces rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: wiring starts with no schematic to follow
anti_rework_rules.example: breadboarding from memory and miswiring a power rail

anti_rework_rules.rule: prove a circuit on a breadboard before committing to solder
anti_rework_rules.rationale: soldering an unproven circuit is expensive, hard-to-reverse rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a circuit is soldered before its behavior is verified
anti_rework_rules.example: soldering a board then finding the bias was wrong

anti_rework_rules.rule: size power and select the board before planning pins, buses, and I/O
anti_rework_rules.rationale: I/O planned for the wrong board or rail is redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: pin/bus planning begins before the board and voltage domain are fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: planning 5V interfaces then switching to a 3.3V board

anti_rework_rules.rule: design a rated, protected driver stage before driving any actuator
anti_rework_rules.rationale: direct or unprotected drive destroys parts and the MCU
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an actuator is energized with no driver or flyback path
anti_rework_rules.example: driving a relay coil from a bare pin and frying it

anti_rework_rules.rule: bring up and verify each subsystem before integrating or enclosing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: integrating unverified parts multiplies and hides faults
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: subsystems are enclosed before they pass bring-up
anti_rework_rules.example: boxing up an intermittent joint that is then unreachable

anti_rework_rules.rule: measure expected vs actual before replacing any component
anti_rework_rules.rationale: guess-and-swap replaces good parts and wastes time
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: parts are swapped with no measurement narrowing the fault
anti_rework_rules.example: replacing a sensor when the rail was actually low

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or bring-up review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk_score and safety impact
acceptance_tests: highest-risk and safety defects first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue ordered and no high-risk defect unranked

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix touches a high-coupling node (power, board, topology)
iteration_protocol.detection: trace edges from the changed node
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the change identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is ready to fix
iteration_protocol.detection: map the defect type to its subsystem via repair_routing
acceptance_tests: each repair routed to the correct subsystem

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair changed a locked or high-coupling component
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run validator and re-measure affected nets
acceptance_tests: affected checks re-run and passing
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: revalidation passes with no new failures

iteration_protocol.trigger: evidence about a node's reliability changes (e.g., a part proves flaky)
iteration_protocol.detection: check whether posterior assumptions still hold
acceptance_tests: posterior reflects the new evidence
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no material posterior delta above the revisit threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is high-risk, irreversible, or near a safety red line
iteration_protocol.detection: check risk_if_wrong and irreversibility against thresholds
action: require human review with a decision record
acceptance_tests: no irreversible high-risk action without review
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human decision recorded and acted on

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix or redesign could regress a previously passing subsystem
iteration_protocol.detection: compare current results against the prior accepted baseline
acceptance_tests: no previously passing subsystem now fails

human_review_required_for: first power-up of any real power source or lithium pack
driving a motor or inductive load through a new driver stage
soldering or any irreversible assembly step
